patients.summary: Retired accountant in Westhampton with HTN, T2DM, HLD and CKD 3 who joined in 2019, had stage I right colon cancer resected in 2020, then hypertensive retinopathy, a conduction block, spinal stenosis, Paget disease, giant cell arteritis and acute pancreatitis. Last seen May 2026 for rapid cognitive decline that outside neurology diagnosed as sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Caller: William Wells, wants to transfer care. Says his old doctor in town is cutting back hours and his wife's friend recommended us. On Medicare, has supplement card. Diabetes and blood pressure, sees nobody else regularly right now.
Booked new patient visit 9/17 at 9:00 with PCP. Release signed by pt over portal for prior PCP records; request faxed today.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
41 pages received from prior PCP office (internal medicine, Hampshire County). Covers 2011 to 2019.
Problem list on their records: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, CKD stage 3.
Med list: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: none known.
Screening: colonoscopy 2008 reported normal, no polyps. Pneumococcal polysaccharide noted 2018. No Tdap date found.
Filed to media tab. Flagged for PCP before new patient visit.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with meals

medications.drug: aspirin 81 MG Delayed Release Oral Tablet

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT — establishing care

66 y/o retired accountant here to transfer primary care. Chronic issues: HTN for many years, type 2 DM roughly a decade, high cholesterol, and stage 3 CKD that his old PCP followed with labs. Feels fine. No chest pain, no breathing trouble with yard work, no foot sores. Takes his pills from a weekly organizer his wife set up.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
PSH: none.
FH: father had high blood pressure and coronary disease. Mother had type 2 diabetes. A paternal uncle had colon cancer in his seventies.
SH: married, lives in Westhampton. Retired from accounting. Never smoker. Does not drink.

Prior records reviewed: last colonoscopy 2008, normal. Overdue.

Exam: Well appearing. BP and vitals as recorded. Height 178 cm. Fundi not well seen through undilated pupils. Neck supple, no bruits. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Feet: skin intact, monofilament felt at all sites, DP pulses 2+ both sides. No edema.

A/P
1. Hypertension: at goal on lisinopril + amlodipine. Continue.
2. Type 2 diabetes: on metformin. A1c, urine microalbumin today.
3. CKD 3a: creatinine per old records in the 1.3-1.4 range. Recheck CMP. Avoid NSAIDs, explained.
4. Hyperlipidemia: atorvastatin 40. Lipids today.
5. Health maintenance: Tdap today. Hep C screen today. Colonoscopy referral to GI given the 11-year gap and uncle's history. He would rather not go before the holidays; will let GI call him.
Return in 3 months.

documents.title: Your recent labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Mr. Wells, your bloodwork is back. Kidney function is about where your old office had it, stable stage 3. Sugar control (A1c) is good. Cholesterol on atorvastatin is fine. Hepatitis C screen negative, urine protein normal. No changes. See you in December.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu vaccine given IM left deltoid. Pt tolerated. No prior reactions. VIS reviewed.

documents.title: GI scheduling
documents.author: MA
documents.body: GI office called: pt was offered 11/21 for colonoscopy and asked to push to after New Year. They will call him in January. Pt aware per GI. FYI PCP.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here for 3 mo f/u. No complaints. Checks BP at the pharmacy machine sometimes, 130s. Not checking sugars, which is reasonable on metformin alone.
Colonoscopy still to be booked after the holidays, he says.
Exam: BP as charted. Heart regular, lungs clear. Feet intact, no edema.
Labs from September reviewed with him.
Plan: no changes. A1c and BMP in spring. RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax for 90-day supplies: metformin 1000, lisinopril 10, amlodipine 5, atorvastatin 40. Last visit 12/17. Sent per protocol, 1 refill each.

documents.title: Procedure postponed
documents.author: RN
documents.body: GI office cancelled pt's 3/26 colonoscopy; elective procedures on hold because of COVID. They will rebook when they reopen. Called pt, he knows. No bleeding, no change in bowels, no weight loss. Told him to call if any of that changes.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from home, wife helped set up the tablet. Consent for telehealth given.
Staying home, walking the road most days. Home cuff readings he read off: 128/78, 134/82, 131/79. Weight on bathroom scale 181 lb.
No symptoms. Meds unchanged, enough on hand.
Labs deferred until the lab draw station reopens normally.
Colonoscopy will be rescheduled by GI when they resume.
Plan: continue all. Labs in early summer. Video or in person in 5 months.

documents.title: Colonoscopy report (outside GI)
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY — COLONOSCOPY REPORT
Date of procedure: 06/10/2020
Indication: screening, last exam 2008; second-degree relative with colon cancer.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care. Prep: good.
Findings: cecum reached, appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve identified. In the ascending colon, an irregular partly circumferential mass about 3 cm, friable, non-obstructing; multiple cold forceps biopsies taken and the site tattooed distally. Remainder of colon to rectum normal. No other polyps. Retroflexion normal.
Impression: ascending colon mass, suspicious for malignancy. Pathology pending; patient and wife informed today. Will contact referring PCP with results.
Medications/allergies reviewed: NKDA.

documents.title: Pathology, ascending colon biopsies (outside)
documents.author: pathology
documents.body:
Specimen: ascending colon mass, biopsies.
Diagnosis: invasive adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated.
Mismatch repair proteins: intact expression (MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6).

documents.title: Results call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Mr. Wells with his wife on speaker. Biopsy shows colon cancer. GI had already told them it looked suspicious so not a total surprise, but hard to hear. Answered questions as best I could. Next steps: staging CT scans and CEA, then surgical consult. Referrals placed urgently to general surgery and oncology. GI is ordering the CTs. Will call him after scans. He has my cell through the practice line if he needs it.

reports.text: CT chest with contrast. Indication: staging, colon adenocarcinoma. Lungs clear without nodule or mass. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. No pleural effusion. Heart normal in size. Bones without suspicious lesion.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of metastatic disease in the chest.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Reduced-volume IV contrast given for renal function. Mild wall thickening in the ascending colon at the known tumor site with a tattoo marker distally; no pericolonic stranding. No enlarged mesenteric or retroperitoneal nodes. Liver without focal lesion. Gallbladder, pancreas, spleen, adrenals normal. Kidneys normal in size, no hydronephrosis. No ascites. Bladder and prostate unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Known ascending colon primary. No lymphadenopathy or distant metastasis.

documents.title: CT staging (outside)
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: See attached reports. CEA drawn same morning: within normal limits.

reports.text: Right colon and terminal ileum, resection: adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, 3.1 cm, ascending colon. Tumor invades into the muscularis propria. No lymphovascular invasion identified. Proximal, distal and radial margins negative. Nineteen lymph nodes examined, all negative.
reports.conclusion: Adenocarcinoma of ascending colon, pT2 N0, margins negative.

documents.title: Discharge summary (outside hospital)
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — SURGERY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 07/08/2020, discharged 07/11/2020.
Procedure 07/08: laparoscopic-assisted right hemicolectomy with primary ileocolic anastomosis for ascending colon adenocarcinoma.
Course: uncomplicated. Diet advanced day 2, bowel function by day 3. Metformin held while NPO and resumed on discharge. Discharge home with wife.
Final pathology: adenocarcinoma invading the muscularis propria (pT2), 0 of 19 lymph nodes involved (pN0), margins negative. AJCC stage I.
Follow-up: surgical clinic 2 weeks; medical oncology to discuss surveillance.
Discharge meds: home medications unchanged.
Allergies: NKDA.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, two weeks after right hemicolectomy. Saw surgery yesterday, incisions healing, they were happy.
Eating normally, bowels loose for a week then settling. Pain mostly gone. Back on all his regular meds including metformin. Sugars not checked.
Path reviewed: stage I, nodes negative. He was relieved.
Oncology appointment in August.
Plan: no changes. BMP when he is out for his oncology visit or at next in-person.

documents.title: Medical oncology consultation (outside)
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE MEDICAL ONCOLOGY — CONSULT LETTER
Seen 08/05/2020 for stage I (pT2 N0) adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon after laparoscopic right hemicolectomy 07/08/2020. MMR proficient. Pre-op CEA normal; staging CTs without metastasis.
He is recovering well. Exam unremarkable, incisions healed.
Recommendation: no adjuvant chemotherapy is indicated for stage I disease. Surveillance: clinic visit with CEA yearly, colonoscopy at one year from surgery.
Family history reviewed: no first-degree relative with colorectal cancer; a paternal uncle had colon cancer in his 70s.
Thank you for this referral.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
In person for the first time since his surgery. Feels back to normal, walking 2 miles. Appetite good, weight down a few pounds and now stable.
Oncology: no chemo, yearly visits, colonoscopy next summer. Updated problem list to history of colon cancer.
BP fine at home. No hypoglycemia symptoms.
Exam: abdomen with healed laparoscopic incisions, soft, nontender. Heart and lungs normal. Feet: monofilament intact, pulses good.
Plan: A1c, BMP, lipids today. Continue meds. Flu shot in October with nurse.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Fluzone high-dose given IM right deltoid. Masked, screened at door, afebrile. Tolerated.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Initial Medicare AWV.
Health risk assessment reviewed: lives with wife in their own home, drives, handles finances (still does a few neighbors' tax returns as favors). No falls. Hearing and vision self-rated fine. Sleep ok. PHQ-2 negative.
Advance directive: has health care proxy (wife); copy requested.
Screening: colorectal per oncology/GI surveillance. Hep C done. Tdap 2019. Shingrix 1 of 2 done at pharmacy. Pneumococcal: PPSV23 2018 per old records; conjugate vaccine to discuss next year.
Exam: BP as charted, BMI 26. Normal general exam.
Labs from September reviewed, stable kidney function.
Plan: second Shingrix in 2-6 months at pharmacy. COVID vaccine when his age group is eligible. RTC 3-4 months.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Fully vaccinated now, glad to be out. Doing well. Walking. No GI symptoms, normal BMs since surgery.
BP at home 120s-130s.
Exam: no distress. RRR. Lungs clear. Abd soft. No edema. Feet intact.
A/P: DM stable, HTN at goal, CKD 3a stable on recent labs. Labs today. Oncology one-year visit in June. Continue. RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Oncology follow-up letter (outside)
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE MEDICAL ONCOLOGY — FOLLOW-UP
Visit date: 06/30/2021
Mr. Wells, 68, returns a year out from his right hemicolectomy for stage I colon adenocarcinoma. He has had no new symptoms and says he has felt well since the operation.
Other history: hypertension (lisinopril, amlodipine), type 2 diabetes (metformin), hyperlipidemia, CKD stage 3. Meds also atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81. NKDA.
Never smoker, no alcohol. Retired accountant. No colorectal cancer in a first-degree relative.
Vitals normal. Exam: unremarkable, no adenopathy, abdomen benign.
Labs: Hgb 13.8, WBC 7.2, platelets 250. Na 140, K 4.2, fasting glucose 98. CEA within normal limits.
Assessment: no evidence of recurrence. Plan: surveillance colonoscopy due now (GI arranging), annual visit and CEA.

documents.title: Colonoscopy report (outside GI)
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GI — COLONOSCOPY
Date: 07/20/2021. Indication: surveillance, 1 year after right hemicolectomy for stage I colon cancer.
Prep excellent. Ileocolic anastomosis reached and examined: healthy, patent, no recurrence. Neo-terminal ileum normal. Remaining colon and rectum normal. No polyps.
Recommendation: repeat colonoscopy in 3 years.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six-month check. Colonoscopy in July was clean, oncology happy.
Feels fine. Mentions his eyes are "not what they were" for reading road signs, will go over at his wellness visit.
BP okay today. No hypoglycemia. Diet unchanged.
Exam: heart regular, lungs clear, ext without edema, feet normal sensation.
Plan: labs in December with AWV. Flu and COVID booster in October. Continue meds.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu L deltoid. Pfizer booster R deltoid (eligible, >6 months from series). Observed 15 minutes, fine.

orders.reason: abnormal vision screen, diabetic eye exam

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subsequent AWV plus chronic f/u.
Vision: for several months notices his side vision isn't as sharp and lights at night have a fuzzy halo. No sudden change, no eye pain. Never needed glasses. Last eye exam he can't remember, years.
Snellen today reduced both eyes compared with what he expected (see vitals flowsheet). No other new issues.
PHQ-2 negative. No falls. Independent.
Exam: undilated fundi poorly seen. Otherwise normal. Feet intact.
A/P
1. Abnormal vision screen with peripheral vision complaints: ophthalmology referral for dilated exam; also due for diabetic eye exam.
2. DM/HTN/CKD: labs today.
3. Prevention: pneumococcal conjugate next visit.
